hints: The maximum candy count is k, and each of n children independently receives a uniform integer from 1 to k.
The maximum equals r when all choices are at most r, minus the chance they are all at most r-1.
Sum r times the probability that the maximum equals r.
analogy: Use cumulative probabilities: all children stay below a threshold with probability (threshold/k)^n.
example: For one child, the maximum is uniform 1..k, so its expected value is (k+1)/2.
correctness: The event max<=r means every independent child chooses one of r values, so its probability is (r/k)^n; differencing gives exact max probabilities.
complexity: O(k log n) using exponentiation by squaring per r, O(1) extra space.
algorithm: For each possible maximum r=1..k, P(max=r)=(r/k)^n-((r-1)/k)^n. Sum r*P(max=r) using floating-point arithmetic and print six decimals.
